title: Minimum Number of Steps to Make Two Strings Anagram II
summary: Given two strings s and t, determine the fewest steps needed to append characters to either string so they both become anagrams of each other.
statement: Given two strings s and t, determine the fewest steps needed to append characters to either string so they both become anagrams of each other. An anagram shares the same characters in any order.
constraints: One step appends one lowercase letter to either string.
After all steps, the two strings must have identical character counts.
Return the minimum number of appended characters.
hints: Each character can be balanced independently because appending never removes an existing count.
For each letter, append exactly the absolute difference between its two counts.
Build two counters and sum abs(count_s-count_t) across their key union.
Every imbalance requires that many additions to the deficient side, and performing those additions makes the count vectors equal.
editorial: Every imbalance requires that many additions to the deficient side, and performing those additions makes the count vectors equal.

tests.explanation: The total absolute difference across character counts is seven, so seven appends are necessary.
The strings already contain the same letters with the same counts, so return zero.
